hero.headline: Precision Dental Care, On Your Schedule.
hero.subheadline: From root canals to braces to oral surgery, V Smile brings specialist-level dentistry to Madhanandapuram — with evening and Sunday appointments built for people who can't take time off during the day.

about.title: Specialist dentistry, not just checkups
body: V Smile Dental Clinic was built around a simple idea: patients in Madhanandapuram shouldn't have to travel across Chennai to see a specialist for a root canal, a wisdom tooth extraction, or braces. Our team covers endodontics, oral surgery, orthodontics, and pediatric dentistry under one roof, so referrals to a different clinic are rarely necessary.

We also know most people can't take a weekday afternoon off for a dental visit. That's why V Smile runs as an evening and weekend-focused clinic — open until 9:30 PM every day, including Sundays — so working professionals and families can get specialist care without missing work or school.

blogPosts.title: Root Canal Myths, Debunked by a Dentist
blogPosts.excerpt: Root canals have a reputation they don't deserve. Here's what the procedure is actually like, from someone who performs them every week.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Arvind Shanmugam
content: Ask most people what they think of when they hear "root canal" and you'll get a wince. It's one of the most feared phrases in dentistry — and almost entirely undeserved. As someone who performs root canal treatment regularly, I want to clear up a few persistent myths.

Myth one: root canals are extremely painful. In reality, the procedure is done under local anesthesia, and the pain patients associate with root canals is usually the infection that made the treatment necessary in the first place — not the treatment itself. Most patients tell me it feels similar to getting a filling.

Myth two: it's better to just pull the tooth. Extraction might seem simpler, but a root canal preserves your natural tooth, which keeps your bite, jawbone, and neighboring teeth healthier long-term. Replacing an extracted tooth with an implant or bridge is usually more expensive and more involved than the root canal would have been.

Myth three: recovery takes a long time. Most patients are back to normal eating within a day or two once the permanent crown is placed. There may be mild soreness immediately after, easily managed with over-the-counter pain relief.

If you're putting off a root canal out of fear, my advice is simple: come in for a consultation and let's talk through exactly what your specific case involves. Waiting usually makes the underlying problem worse, not better.
